name: Nizari Ismaili state
alt: Nizari Ismaili State of Persia and Syria

predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: Alamut ('captured from Mahdi in 1090'), then Rudkhan, Gerdkuh and Lambsar, Seljuk-held castles

successors.name: Ulus of Hülegü
successors.text: the Persian strongholds: Alamut 1256, Lambsar 1257, Gerdkuh December 1270

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: the Syrian castles: Masyaf 1270, al-Ullaiqah, ar-Rusafa and Khawabi 1271, al-Kahf last in 1273

ledger.x: 1090: Hassan-i Sabbah captures Alamut without violence.
1096: the Assassins seize Rudkhan.
1100: Gerdkuh passes to the Nizaris.
1101: the Seljuk sieges begin.
1102: Lambsar in Assassin hands by this year.
1118: the Seljuk sieges end ('From 1101 to 1118'); the page records no decisive result, and Sanjar's forces struck again at Quhistan, Nishapur and Rudbar in 1126 without a decisive outcome.
1133: the Assassins buy al-Qadmus.
ledger.cp: Saif al-Mulk ibn Amrun (emir of al-Kahf)

ledger.x: 1138: al-Kahf is ceded.
1140: the Assassins acquire Masyaf ('the acquisition of the castle at Masyaf in 1140'); the page names no seller.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1141: the Assassins acquire Qala'at al-Khawabi, 'known to the Crusaders as La Coible, in 1141'; the page names no seller.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1157: the Assassins occupy the castle at Shaizar a second time, after the 1157 earthquake; they had earlier 'occupied the fortress at Shaizar held by the Banu Munqidh' until a local rebellion drove them out.
1158: Nur ad-Din takes the Shaizar castle, 'incorporating a castle at Shaizar that they had occupied after the 1157 earthquake into his territory'.
Undated, placed at 1162: 'Sinan also captured the castle of al-'Ullaiqah at Aleika, near Tartus' and oversaw 'the refurbishing of the fortress of ar-Rusafa'.
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1253: the Mongols besiege Gerdkuh.
1256: Alamut falls to the Mongols.
1256: Rudkhan's fate is on no page opened (seized 1096); it is closed with Alamut at confidence 1.
1257: Lambsar falls to the Mongols.
1270: Baibars takes Masyaf.
1270: Gerdkuh surrenders, 'the last Nizari stronghold in Persia'.
1270: the Mongol siege of Gerdkuh ends on 15 December.
1271: Baibars' forces seize al-'Ullaiqah and ar-Rusafa; Khawabi 'also fell that year'.
1273: al-Kahf, 'the last stronghold', falls to the Mamluks; 'within two years Gerdkuh and all of the Assassin fortresses were held by the sultan'.
1273: the last Nizari castle falls and the state ends.

wars.name: Seljuk attacks on the Nizari fortresses
wars.outcome: 'From 1101 to 1118, attacks and sieges were made on the fortresses'; no fortress was lost on the page's account (the Tabas siege was lifted in 1101).

wars.name: Saladin's siege of Masyaf
wars.outcome: 'In 1176, Saladin laid siege to Masyaf' but lifted it; no territory changed hands (Sinan page).

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Nizari state in Persia
wars.outcome: Kitbuqa began assaulting fortresses in 1253; Rukn al-Din Khurshah surrendered at Maymun-Diz (19 November 1256) and Alamut fell in December 1256; Lambsar fell in 1257; Gerdkuh surrendered on 15 December 1270 after a siege since May 1253.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of the Syrian Assassin castles
wars.outcome: Baibars took Masyaf in 1270 (1267 in another section of the page), al-'Ullaiqah, ar-Rusafa and Khawabi in 1271 and al-Kahf, the last stronghold, in 1273.

certainty.note: A network of mountain fortresses and the land around them, with no frontier line on any page opened: Persian castles in the Alamut valley (Rudbar), Gerdkuh near Damghan and Quhistan, Syrian castles in the Jabal Bahra/Nusayriyah mountains.
